The petitioner is before this Court seeking the following prayers:
"a. Issue a writ, Order or direction in the nature of mandamus to the Respondents to be pleased to act in strict compliance of the Notification bearing No.HD 119 PRA 2018, Bengaluru, dated 21.04.2020 produced as Annexure-A and be further pleased to direct the respondents to consider the case of the petitioner for premature release in terms of the Annexure-A. NC: 2025:KHC:15132 b. Issue a Writ, Order or direction in the nature of mandamus to the Respondents to release the petitioner on parole till the decision of the Government as per the dicta of the Hon'ble Apex Court rendered in Rashidul Jafar Vs State of Uttar Pradesh dated 06-09-2022 produced as Annexure C and also the order passed by this Hon'ble court in WP No. 1300/2023 dated 02-03- 2023 produced as ANNEXURE-D in the interest of justice and equity.
c. Pass such other orders/ directions considering the facts and circumstances of the case together as to costs in the interest of justice."

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties herein are referred to as per their status before the trial Court.

sentences.text: 3. Brief facts leading to this appeal are that Chikkaballapura Rural Police submitted charge-sheet against the accused 1 to 7 for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 304B, 306 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code and Sections 3, 4 and 6 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: It is alleged by the p r o s e c u t i o n t h a t , t h e m a r r i a g e o f a p p e l l a n t v i c t i m - G e e t h a , d a u g h t e r o f
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: complainant-Chandrashekaraiah was solemnized on 28th April, 2005 at Chikkaballapura as per Hindu rites and customs.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: Prior to marriage, there was negotiation, in which family members of the appellant demanded jewels for bride and the groom and dowry of Rs.2,00,000/-.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: Finally, it was settled that complainant shall give Rs.1,00,000/- as dowry, accordingly 15 days prior to the marriage, complainant delivered Rs.1,00,000/- to the father of the appellant.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: After marriage, the couple lived cordially in the matrimonial home.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: Meanwhile, she became pregnant and was suffering from stomach pain, appellant took her to hospital for treatment and brought her to parents house.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: Thereafter, she gave birth to a baby.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: Despite informing, accused did not visit her in the hospital.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: The complainant gave his daughter a mobile and cash of Rs.4,000/-
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: After 20 days, appellant visited her and took away cash and mobile phone.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: Four months after delivery she was taken to matrimonial house, where she was subjected to mental and physical harassment, demanding further dowry in the form of cash and lands.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: In the meanwhile, again she became pregnant, but pregnancy was terminated by administering with some tablets, on account of which she suffered stomach pain.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: Thereafter, all the accused subjected her to cruelty demanding money for construction of house and also to get lands transferred to her name.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: The complainant paid Rs.50,000/- and despite receiving the said amount, his daughter was subjected to cruelty.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: 4. On 25th February, 2009 at about 09.00 am, appellant, over phone, requested the son of the complainant to come to his house.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: When he went, he saw the victim crying and when he asked her to come to her parents house, she replied that she would rather die in her matrimonial house but will not go to her parents house.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: On 27th March, 2009, at 7.00 pm the appellant informed the complainant over phone that something had happened to Geetha and asked him to come to Government Hospital, when he and his family members went to hospital, the dead body of the victim Geetha was brought in an ambulance.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: Complainant suspected that accused might have subjected his daughter to cruelty demanding dowry and might have killed her by giving poison.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: Based on the said complaint, the above case came to be registered.

sentences.text: During the course of prosecution evidence, Exhibits D1 to D4 were marked.

sentences.text: 8. Having heard the arguments on both sides, the trial Court acquitted accused 1 to 3 and 5 to 7 for offences under Section 498A, 304B, 306 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code and Section 3, 4 and 6 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

sentences.text: The trial Court convicted accused No.4/appellant herein for the offence under Sections 498A and 306 of Indian Penal Code and sentenced the accused to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of two years and to pay fine of Rs.2,000/- for the offence under Section 488A of Indian Penal Code.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: Further, accused No.4 was sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 8 years and to pay fine of Rs.5,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 306 of Indian Penal Code.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the judgment of conviction and order on sentence, the accused No.4 has preferred this appeal.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: 9. Learned Counsel, Sri S. Balakrishnan appearing for the appellant would submit that, the trial Court has held that there are no materials against the appellant for the offence punishable under Section 304B of Indian Penal Code and Sections 3, 4 and 6 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: The trial Court ought to have extended the same benefit to the appellant for the offence under Sections 498A and 306 of IPC, but has erroneously convicted him for the said offence.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: He would submit that PW1-Chandrasekharaiah-father of the deceased, has stated in his evidence that after marriage with the appellant, they were living cordially.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: His entire evidence indicates that he is an hearsay witness.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: He had not deposed anything regarding his personal knowledge of matrimonial life of his daughter-Geetha.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: PW1 has not deposed regarding the demand or harassment on the part of the accused No.4.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: PWs2 to 4 are not consistent in their evidence and they have not spoken regarding matrimonial life of deceased-Geetha.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: Independent witnesses have not supported the case of the prosecution.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: Hence, there is no corroboration of evidence of PWs1 to 4.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: Further, it is admitted that PWs1 to 4 do not, in any way, establish that appellant treated the deceased with cruelty of such nature as defined under Section 498A Indian Penal Code.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: The evidence of PWs1 to 4 also do not establish any nature of cruel treatment on the part of the appellant, which abetted the deceased to commit suicide.
sentences._hearing_file: Sri Venkatesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 January, 2026.json

opennyai_summary.final__arguments:
9. Learned Counsel, Sri S. Balakrishnan appearing for the appellant would submit that, the trial Court has held that there are no materials against the appellant for the offence punishable under Section 304B of Indian Penal Code and Sections 3, 4 and 6 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The trial Court ought to have extended the same benefit to the appellant for the offence under Sections 498A and 306 of IPC, but has erroneously convicted him for the said offence.
PWs2 to 4 are not consistent in their evidence and they have not spoken regarding matrimonial life of deceased-Geetha.
Independent witnesses have not supported the case of the prosecution.
Hence, there is no corroboration of evidence of PWs1 to 4.
Further, it is admitted that PWs1 to 4 do not, in any way, establish that appellant treated the deceased with cruelty of such nature as defined under Section 498A Indian Penal Code.
The evidence of PWs1 to 4 also do not establish any nature of cruel treatment on the part of the appellant, which abetted the deceased to commit suicide.
10. To substantiate his argument, learned counsel relied on the following decisions:
i) PRAKASH AND OTHERS v. STATE OF MAHARASHTRA AND ANOTHER RENDERED IN CRIMINAL APPEAL NO... OF 2024 ARISING OUT OF SLP (CRL.) NO.1073 OF 2023 DECIDED ON 20.12.2024;
